docs.title: ORIGINAL BIASES & DESIGN PREFERENCES
docs.text:
Extracted: 2026-02-26 | Source: GENESIS Chat (eb53e82c) & Evolution v1-v3

These are the "calibration zeros" of the Rhea project. They represent the foundational biases and cognitive preferences of the Product Owner (Rex) and the original system architecture.

docs.title: 1. Communication & Persona Biases
docs.text:
• Guide over Sage: The system must act as a tutor or guide, not an all-knowing sage.
  • Intent over Literalism: Respond to what the person means, not just what they say.
  • Bias Acknowledgement: AI must acknowledge its editorial choices and stop masking them as "objective truth" (Anti-Naive Realism).
  • Language: All internal memory and relay entries are stored in English, regardless of the input language.

docs.title: 2. Infrastructure & Cultural Biases
docs.text:
• Anti-Gregorian Default: Recognizes that Gregorian-only timestamps are a cultural choice, not a neutral one. Adapt to user-specific calendars (e.g., Hijri).
  • Body before Mind: Prioritizes sensory and biological regulation (HRV, light) over cognitive decision-making in the morning.
  • Holographic Consistency: Prioritizes 3-layered auditability (Git / Local / Cloud) over theoretical database atomicity.

docs.title: 3. The 8-Level Symbolic Power Framework
docs.text: The system aims to monitor and potentially intervene across these 8 levels of user perception: 1. Ontology (What exists) 2. Taxonomy (How it is categorized) 3. Causality (What causes what) 4. Temporality (How time is perceived) 5. Spatiality (How space is organized) 6. Subjectivity (Who the user is) 7. Thinkability (What is allowed to be thought) 8. Aesthetics (What feels "right" or "legitimate")

docs.title: 4. D-Metric Logic Baseline (v3.1)
docs.text:
• Logarithmic Dampening: Success should not be penalized (Success-based bloat).
  • Square-Root Friction: Debt compounds non-linearly (Compounding friction).
  • Inverse Intelligence: Efficiency is the ultimate reward (Intelligence density).

Note: This file serves as the "Calibration Zero" for all future system upgrades and adversarial reviews.

docs.title: Rhea — Reflection Log
docs.text: Failure memory + lessons learned. Consult before repeating similar tasks.

docs.title: Format
docs.text: Each entry records: what happened, why it failed, root cause, and the fix. This log is part of the self-improvement loop (ADR-011, technique #5: Failure Memory).

docs.title: Entry 001: Entire.io auto-commit strategy doesn't inject trailers (2026-02-13)
docs.text:
What happened: Entire.io was configured with auto-commit strategy. Expected Entire-Checkpoint trailers on user commits. Trailers were missing.

Root cause: auto-commit creates separate commits for checkpoint data. Only manual-commit strategy adds trailers to the user's own commits via the commit-msg hook.

Fix: Switched to manual-commit in .entire/settings.local.json. Verified trailer injection works.

Lesson: Read Entire.io docs carefully before assuming behavior. The strategy names are misleading — "auto" doesn't mean "automatic trailer injection."

docs.title: Entry 002: commit-msg hook not executable (2026-02-13)
docs.text:
What happened: commit-msg hook existed at .git/hooks/commit-msg but wasn't being invoked.

Root cause: File permissions were -rw------- (no execute bit). Git hooks require +x.

Fix: chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

Lesson: Always check file permissions when hooks aren't firing. This is a common gotcha with git hooks.

docs.title: Entry 003: Stale metrics in memory_metrics.json (2026-02-14)
docs.text:
What happened: Memory benchmark reported core_docs_kb as 124 in metrics file, but actual measurement was 24KB.

Root cause: Metrics were recorded in Session 9 and never updated as docs were compacted/reorganized. The D calculation was inflated (91.96 vs actual 62.7).

Fix: Updated all fields in metrics/memory_metrics.json with live measurements. Added benchmark script to automatically detect stale values.

Lesson: Metrics must be updated after every structural change. The benchmark script now checks for staleness — run it after every session that modifies docs.

docs.title: Entry 004: VM cannot run macOS-only tools (2026-02-13)
docs.text:
What happened: Attempted to run entire checkpoint create from the Cowork VM. Command not found.

Root cause: Entire CLI is installed on macOS, not in the Linux VM. The VM sees the repo via FUSE mount but doesn't have macOS tools.

Fix: Use osascript via Desktop Commander to run macOS commands. Path mapping: VM /sessions/vibrant-zealous-allen/mnt/rh.1/ → macOS /Users/sa/rh.1/.

Lesson: Any tool that must run on macOS (entire, git with hooks, SSH with keys) needs to go through osascript. Keep a clear mental model of VM vs macOS boundaries.

docs.title: Entry 005: Cowork commits bypass Entire.io session lifecycle (2026-02-14)
docs.text:
What happened: After switching to Cowork for commits (Sessions 14-16), zero Entire.io checkpoints appeared on the dashboard despite 4 successful git commits. The last checkpoint was from a Claude Code session 17+ hours prior.

Root cause: Entire.io's manual-commit strategy requires an active agent session to inject Entire-Checkpoint trailers. The lifecycle is: session-start → prepare-commit-msg (trailer injection) → git commit → post-commit (condense) → session-stop. Cowork commits via osascript do shell script "git commit..." bypass this lifecycle entirely — no session-start fires, so prepare-commit-msg has no session context.

Evidence: .entire/logs/entire.log showed last session with checkpoint was da10a451 at 2026-02-13T23:58. After that: 4 commits with zero log entries, zero trailers. All 4 were Cowork commits.

Fix: Created scripts/rhea_commit.sh wrapper (ADR-013, Tribunal-002) that explicitly triggers entire hooks git session-start before and session-stop after every commit. Use this wrapper instead of raw git commit from Cowork.

Lesson: When tools depend on a specific lifecycle (session hooks, daemon events), verify that ALL execution contexts trigger that lifecycle. Cowork and Claude Code have different execution models — what works in one may silently fail in the other. Always check the log trail when expected side-effects don't appear.

docs.title: RheaKit API Structure
docs.text: Framework: RheaKit (Play Framework v4.x) Version: 4.2.0+ Platform: iOS/macOS SwiftUI Architecture: MVVM + Reactive Store Pattern

docs.title: RheaAPI - Central HTTP Client
docs.text:
public final class RheaAPI: @unchecked Sendable

Key Methods: - get(_:auth:) - Generic GET with optional auth - post(_:body:auth:) - Generic POST with JSON body - getJSON(_:auth:) - GET returning parsed dictionary - health() - System health snapshot - agents() - Agent status enumeration - history(limit:) - SQL-backed conversation history - radio(limit:) - Agent radio communications - proofs() - Immutable proof database - ontologies() - Knowledge graph ontologies - models() - Infrastructure model providers

Authentication Flow: 1. JWT Bearer token (preferred) 2. API Key fallback (dev-bypass for local) 3. Keychain storage for persistence

docs.title: RheaStore - Reactive State Management
docs.text:
@MainActor
public final class RheaStore: ObservableObject

Data Tiers: - Core (polled every 5s): agents, health, proof count - On-demand (fetched when needed): history, radio, proofs, ontologies - Ephemeral (never cached): SSE streams, active dialogs

Key Properties: - @Published var agents: [AgentDTO] - @Published var health: HealthSnapshot? - @Published var connectionAlive: Bool - @Published var proofCount: Int

Recovery Mechanism: Cellular stress response pattern for cloud restarts: 1. Membrane integrity (server alive check) 2. Core metabolism (SQL-backed data refresh) 3. Clear damaged state (stale counters) 4. Resume normal polling
